<thought>To meet the constraints, I designed a short (3‑step) retrosynthesis. The key disconnections are:
1. Formation of the sulfonamide from a commercially available 4‑fluorobenzenesulfonyl chloride and an amine intermediate.
2. Construction of the amine intermediate by a Buchwald‑Hartwig C‑N coupling of a brominated polycyclic aryl bromide (which already contains the fused bicyclic core) with N‑Boc‑piperazine.
3. The N‑Boc‑piperazine is itself a commercial building block, so no further steps are needed.

All leaf molecules (4‑fluorobenzenesulfonyl chloride, the polycyclic aryl bromide, and N‑Boc‑piperazine) are commercially available and inexpensive, keeping the total cost well below $9999. The route uses only three reaction steps, well within the six‑step limit.</thought>
